about: An arrival's record's fields as a listen's filter reads them: by the names the program writes. A module may key its records by its own field ids (email keys `Subject` as `subject`), so a host reads each record the arrival carries, its landing and its parents, by the catalog's names before judging it: `fieldIds` is the record type's position's `fieldIds` in the catalog (name → id, only where the two differ), `fields` the record as its module delivered it, and `named` what the judge is handed. Each name takes the value its id holds, read off the record as delivered (so two fields whose names are each other's ids swap), as a run reading the field through its module does; a name whose id the record does not hold is left as it came; every key the record came with is kept. Held by listen-fire's Rust (crates/movement-engine/src/listen_judge.rs, named_fields) and the engine's TypeScript (listen_plans.ts, namedFields).

cases.case: an email keyed by its module's ids is read by the names a listen writes
a field the record does not hold stays absent, never null
a field whose id holds null is read as null
a record that also carries the name is read by its id, as the run reads it
a record that carries only the name keeps it
two fields whose names are each other's ids swap, each read off the record as delivered
a type whose module keys its fields by their names is read as it came
